For this study, TEMPO also provides a vehicle-level weekly EV charging time series consistent with the weekly mobility demand profiles using different charging strategies. The unmanaged charging scenario in this study uses TEMPO’s Immediate charging strategy, which assumes that vehicles plug in and charge after every trip until they are fully charged or until another trip begins. (2022a). 2.2 Individual Electric Vehicle Flexibility Models We represent the ability to flexibly schedule EV charging for inflexible vehicle trips by pairing a deferred charging strategy with the Immediate charging strategy for the same vehicle. The deferred strategy is the most delayed charging profile that still enables all trips, whereas the Immediate strategy is, by definition, the earliest possible charging. Figure 1 shows state of charge (SOC) profiles for one vehicle-week labeled Immediate, Delayed, and Min Charges & Delayed. Pairing the Immediate profile with the Delayed profile defines “within-session” flexibility, which assumes the number of charging sessions and the amount of energy delivered in each charging session stay the same, but energy delivery can be scheduled across the entire vehicle dwell period. Pairing the Immediate profile with the Min Charges & Delayed strategy allows more flexible “within-week” charging deferral. This study assumes ubiquitous charger access for all strategies, that dwelling vehicles can charge at the power level of the last charger used in the Immediate strategy, and that all charging strategies for all sample vehicles start and end each week with full batteries.
